metaDescription: Game flow, win conditions and all roles at a glance
title: Rules
intro: Werewolf by the Unified Ruleset — explained briefly so that everyone sits down at the table with the same rules.

about.title: What it's about
about.intro: Werewolves are hiding in a village. Everyone is secretly given a role and so belongs to a side:
about.village: <hl>Village</hl> — finds the werewolves and eliminates them by vote.
about.werewolves: <hl>Werewolves</hl> — secretly eat villagers at night and disguise themselves as harmless neighbors by day.
about.loners: <hl>Loners</hl> — pursue their own goal and win alone.
about.ambiguous: <hl>Ambiguous</hl> — can switch sides over the course of the game.

setup.title: Setup
setup.moderator: One person is the <hl>moderator</hl>: doesn't play, knows all the roles, guides everyone through night and day, and has the final say on rules questions.
setup.cards: The role cards are dealt face down. Everyone looks at their card in secret and shows it to nobody.
setup.recommendation: Recommendation: 2–3 werewolves for up to 12 players, 3–4 above that.

night.title: The night
night.sleep: Everyone closes their eyes. The moderator wakes the roles one at a time in a fixed order.
night.act: Whoever is woken acts silently by pointing and nodding, then goes back to sleep.
night.firstNight: On the first night, additional roles wake up that set up the game — such as Cupid, the Thief or the Wild Child.
night.wolves: The werewolves wake up together and agree on a victim. They may not eat another werewolf.

day.title: The day
day.wake: Everyone wakes up and the moderator announces who died in the night. The dead reveal their cards and may not give anything away from now on.
day.mayor: On the first day, the village elects a <hl>mayor</hl>. Their vote counts double, they break ties, and they name a successor when they die.
day.vote: The village discusses and votes. Whoever gets the most votes is lynched, reveals their card and is out of the game. In case of a tie, the mayor decides.
day.nextNight: Then the next night falls — until a win condition is met.
day.startWithDay: If you like, the game can start with a day instead of a night.

death.title: Death, love and chain reactions
death.triggers: Some roles trigger something when they die or don't die so easily: the Hunter takes someone down with them, the Elder survives the first werewolf attack, and a wolf that has eaten the Knight with the Rusty Sword dies of it. Details are listed with the roles.
death.cupid: On the first night, Cupid pairs up two people. If one of them dies, the other dies of grief.
death.lovers: If the lovers belong to different sides, they play together against everyone else and win when only the two of them are left alive.

win.title: Who wins?
win.tieBreak: If several conditions are met at the same time, the one listed higher up applies.

table.title: At the table
table.cards: Never show your own card — talking, bluffing and lying are allowed.
table.night: Don't peek at night and don't make noises that give anything away.
table.dead: The dead stay silent and give no more hints.

intro.werewolves: Wake up at night as a pack, eat a victim together and win together.
intro.villagers: Win with the village. Most have a special ability that helps the village.
intro.ambiguous: Start on one side, but can switch sides or roles over the course of the game.
intro.loners: Pursue their own goal and usually win alone.
